headline: The US Department of Energy has announced a planned $100 billion private investment to turn a former uranium enrichment site in Kentucky into an AI data center and power hub.
score_reason: Stays at the pool score: very large announced project, but a target for 2032 and not yet spent.
importance_line: Kentucky residents and ratepayers are the people the design promises not to burden, and the $100 billion is an announced target with a 2032 timeline, not money already spent.
summary: OilPrice.com reports that Brookfield Asset Management will build a 1.8-gigawatt AI and computing campus at the former Paducah site, while NextEra Energy, a large US power company, develops 2 gigawatts of gas-fired power and 2.6 gigawatts of battery storage, with the buildout targeted for 2032 and about 8,000 construction and 600 permanent jobs. The project is meant to feed spare power back to the regional grid, but the article notes it comes as markets sour on AI infrastructure spending, after Oracle's Project Jupiter in New Mexico stalled and OpenAI paused Stargate UK.
notes: Announcement date not stated in the article; pool time is 15 Oct 2026. Article is by Alex Kimani.
